relevance.rationale: INFRA: file absent from HEAD and the working tree; exists only on origin/claude/upload-bib-papers-2026-05-19 (intake commit 30a6599190). Recovered from git history. Identity confirmed from the document's own header (arXiv:2106.09716, review of optical box traps for ultracold gases, three authors) and matches the seeded key. Exactly one citation site: folio/quantum-observable-universe/observations/bec-vortex-data.md:1, in the opening sentence 'BECs provide the cleanest experimental realisation of quantised vortex dynamics \cite{fetter2009,navon2021}' (plus the same key in bec-vortex-data.ts:14). NOT load-bearing: every numbered datum in that block is sourced to a different reference — circulation quantisation to madison2000, lattice formation to abo-shaeer2001, the Kelvin k=1 frequency 2*pi*6.2 Hz to bretin2003, vortex clustering to gauthier2019 — and none is attributed to this document. Full-text grep of the recovered PDF: 'vortex' 9, 'vortices' 3, 'turbulen*' 9, 'circulation' 1, 'Kelvin' 0. So the document does carry vortex/turbulence material (box-trap turbulence), which keeps the citation defensible as general context, but it is a box-trap review rather than a rotating-BEC/vortex-dynamics review, and the sentence's actual claim is carried by fetter2009. Supporting, not core: read once in passing, results never used.

proposedActions.rationale: The citation is a defensible second general-context pointer next to fetter2009; no corpus claim depends on it. Not worth churn. If bec-vortex-data is ever extended with a homogeneous-gas (box-trap) datum, this is the reference that would then become load-bearing.
